newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht under pressure in line with regionals.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht under pressure in line with regionals.

text.p: The Thai baht fell sharply against the dollar in early Monday trade in line with other battered regional currencies, dealers said.
The baht tumbled to 31.90/32.00 to the dollar early in the domestic market from 31.75/31.85 late on Friday.
"I think the recent turmoil in regional currencies prompted people to switch to the dollar," said one dealer at a European bank.
The Bank of Thailand on Monday said the weighted average interbank exchange rate rose to 31.657 per dollar from 31.558 on Friday.
Dealers said the baht's slide was limited by some dollar selling at the 32 baht/dollar strong resistance.
"We have not seen any central bank intervention yet this morning. The baht's fall was capped at the 32 level," said another dealer.
The Indonesian central bank on Thursday floated the rupiah, triggering its steep fall against the dollar and aggravated volatility of other regional currencies.
Dealers said a limited dollar supply due to sluggish exports and foreign fund inflows also compounded the baht's weakness.
"But the market is quite thin, making it easier to move the (dollar/baht) rate," the dealer said. Dealers said fortnight bank reserves and the value added tax rise tightened liquidity.
The baht traded at 31.90/32.00 to the dollar early offshore against 31.35/31.55 late on Friday.

The one-month dollar/baht swap premium stood at 16/20 satangs early onshore and 25/35 offshore. The overnight interbank rate rose to 13-14 percent early from 12 late on Friday on tighter liquidity, dealers said.
